downtime.interval_note: interval 1 is the resize stop/start; intervals 2 and 3 are the deploy's restart; interval 4 coincides with the first large reply requested from this seat (a short stall of the single-worker service on a cold call, not a hang)
downtime.method: an unauthenticated POST to the public MCP endpoint every 2 s from this seat (a healthy gateway answers 401 itself; a stopped or hung one answers 5xx or nothing), first failed sample to first 401 after it; the span includes the sampler's own 2 s step

access_log.method: journalctl -u opal-gateway between the window's two times, grep -c 'POST /mcp' (the service) and 'POST /probe/' (the listener); the audit lake read object by object (key names start with the record's own UTC time); the same window for both
access_log.note: the journal count includes the unauthenticated POST /mcp probes of this seat's downtime sampler (answered 401) that fell inside the window, counted in sampler_probes_in_the_journal_count; the audit lake records only authenticated calls, so the ratio is read with that subtracted too

audit_failure_counter.method: journalctl -u opal-gateway between 2026-10-20T06:30:30Z and 2026-10-20T07:00:30Z (the access-log window), grep -c 'audit-lake WARN'; the counter value is the last count= those lines print, 0 when there is no line; the counter is read by no route, so the journal line is its only observation
